Nurses' helplessness is a mental concept and is a negative psychological feeling that has the characteristics of anxiety and depression. It occurs when the nurse feels he/she has no control over the situation and cannot change it, her knowledge and care are not helpful for the patients and she/he cannot help the patient further
According to their experience, helplessness is much more enduring than powerlessness, does not decrease with rest and there is no relationship between workload and the intensity of feeling helpless
Helplessness differs from powerlessness and hopelessness, which in some cases have overlapped with these concepts

In the theory of learned helplessness, Seligman et al. said ‘helplessness’ is experienced when a person realizes that his or her response has no effect on the outcome, and as a result of this cognitive error, the motivation to respond is weakened

Helplessness causes numerous physical and psychological symptoms. A helpless nurse experienced anxiety symptoms (muscle tension, headache, loss of appetite and sleeplessness) and, to some extent, depression (loneliness, guilt, crying, self‐blame, apathy and irritability)
Helplessness leads to physical and psychological manifestations and increases medical errors
